new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Normally the stress of nouns and verbs is on the penult. Stress is on the ultima in questions which are marked by either -i 'question morpheme' or -ta 'question morpheme'.
new_statements.citation: SIL PNG [Darryl Wilson]. 2004. Zia Organised Phonology Data. 4 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL. https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/42226
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (text layer, 4 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the Author "SIL PNG Branch", created 20 Sep 2004; page footer "Printed: September 21, 2004"). On p. 2, immediately after the vowel examples, the heading and passage read exactly: "Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) / Normally the stress of nouns and verbs is on the penult. Stress is on the ultima in questions which are marked by either -i 'question morpheme' or -ta 'question morpheme'." The only difference from the report's quote is the PDF's layout line break inside "marked / by". Nothing else on stress in the OPD; p. 3 continues with nasalization, syllable patterns, and orthographic conventions. Reading: fixed: penultimate syllable i…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of nouns and verbs. When a question morpheme (-i or -ta) is suffixed, stress shifts to the final syllable, i.e. the question suffix itself is unstressed but pulls stress onto the last stem syllable (penult-of-word counting the suffix? -- the source says 'ultima', so the final syllable of the question form).
new_statements.exceptions: Stress on the ultima in questions marked by -i or -ta; the qualifier 'normally' implies unstated further exceptions. Corroborated second-hand by Smallhorn 2011: 80 (penultimate stress for 2-3 syllable non-verbs in Zia). Wilson 1980/1981 states Zia lacks the two tones of Suena.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, nouns and verbs; no comment on citation forms or phrase stress. The OPD is a 4-page SIL data sheet, not a full phonology; the same page notes nasalization as the main suprasegmental feature.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD covers Zia proper (villages Zare, Ainse, Siu, Popoe, Kobo, Dona; Morobe Province), i.e. ziaa1250. Wilson 1981 notes a Mawae dialect (~92% cognate) and Ziawe vs Yarawi sub-groups with possible intonational differences but the same language; Mawae is treated by Glottolog under Zia-Mawae. The stress statement is for Zia proper.

sources.note: Section 3.6 Suprasegmentals, p. 80: 'penultimate stress is assumed for two- and three-syllable words (at least in the case of non-verbs), based on the analyses of stress in the present-day languages; Suena, Zia, Binandere, Hunjara, Tafota Baruga, and Korafe all exhibit this pattern.' Second-hand (her Zia sources are Wilson & Oida 1976 and Wilson nd,b OPD); notes verbs may follow different stress rules in daughter languages (Binandere, Korafe); no Zia-specific verb rule given.
